title: Degree one on a genus-zero proper curve gives the projective line
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a proper integral curve over $k$ [def-pc-curve, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume that the canonical map $k\to H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ is an isomorphism and that $H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)=0$, where cohomology is [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. If there is an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module $M$ [def-sc-invertible-module] of degree $\deg_k M=1$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], then $C$ is isomorphic over $k$ to $\mathbf P^1_k$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change].

source.place: Tag 0C6T, lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree, with degree d=1: the resulting closed immersion into the projective line is an isomorphism since its image is one-dimensional.
